title: Weapon
description: Canonical, app-owned weapon record for the FFG Star Wars RPG. Ingested ONCE from OggDude's `weapons` category (480 entries), with every code decoded (via the SWItems maps) and every value coerced at ingest. Replaces the runtime resolvers resolveNpcWeapon (gm/index.html), resolveWeapon (lib/gm/encounterStore.js), and the SWItems decode-at-render functions. LOCKED — verified against BLASTPIS (ranged) + VIBKN (melee), and the decode maps (RANGE_LABELS / QUALITY_NAMES / SKILL_KEY_TO_NAME). The canonical damage model also fixes a live bug: SWItems drops DamageAdd, so catalog melee weapons currently render 'Br+0'; here damage.value comes from DamageAdd. SCOPE (set at Gate 1): personal-scale weapons ONLY. The ingest filters OUT, before validating against this schema: vehicle-scale weapons (Type=='Vehicle' / Gunnery / sensor-scale ranges), ammunition & components (no range / wrNoRange), and non-weapons such as shields (negative Damage). Those belong to the vehicle and items clusters.
$comment: INGEST CONTRACT — OggDude differs from this shape in five ways the pipeline MUST normalize, all verified against BLASTPIS + VIBKN: (1) every numeric value arrives as a STRING ('6','3','400','2') and is coerced to a number, including quality Counts; (2) Qualities arrives as absent | {Quality:{...}} | {Quality:[{...}]} and is normalized to the array below; (3) SkillKey/RangeValue are codes decoded via the same maps SWItems hardcodes today (lift them into the pipeline); (4) Description carries [H3]/[P]/[BR]/[B] markup to decode, and is the field lore-overrides.json overlays; (5) Sources is a list of full book NAMES (no page) mapped onto rules-index pdfs.alias. Damage uses two source fields — see the damage block.

id.description: Stable app-owned id, slugged once from Name (e.g. 'blaster_pistol', 'vibroknife'); dedupe on collision. Unique within the weapon registry. This is what cross-entity references (NPC loadouts, vehicle hardpoints, shop inventory) point at.

_source_key.description: OggDude Key the record was ingested from (e.g. 'BLASTPIS', 'VIBKN'). Traceability/round-trip only; never an app reference — OggDude Keys are unique, which is why dedupe falls back here.

description.description: Decoded from OggDude Description markup at ingest ([H3]/[P]/[BR]/[B] -> clean text/HTML). This is the field the lore-overrides overlay patches; keep extracted text and the overlay cleanly separable so a re-extract never clobbers curation.

skill.description: Canonical skill id, decoded from SkillKey ('RANGLT' -> 'ranged_light', 'MELEE' -> 'melee'). MUST match an id in the Skill registry. Replaces normalizeSkill at runtime, and is one of the signals cross-checked against damage.base.

damage.$comment: FINAL — value-driven, empirically validated against all 480 weapons across three Gate-1 rounds. Skill-class is NOT a reliable discriminator: FFG lightsabers are FLAT-damage, not Brawn+X (16 of 30 lightsaber-skill weapons are flat). RULE, in order: (1) DamageAdd>0 AND Damage 0/absent -> base='brawn', value=DamageAdd (the Brawn-add; VIBKN +1, exotic melee +2/+3); (2) Damage>0 AND DamageAdd>0 -> base='flat', value=Damage, and FLAG (ambiguous both-signal; the 7 MECH demolition charges); (3) else Damage>0 -> base='flat', value=Damage (BLASTPIS 6, Lightsaber 10); (4) else both 0/absent -> SkillKey class is the TIEBREAKER ONLY: melee-class {MELEE,BRAWL,LTSAB/LTSABER} -> 'brawn' value 0 (Brawn+0, e.g. garrote); non-melee -> 'flat' value 0. Skill-class is the both-zero tiebreaker, never the primary discriminator.

value.description: flat: the absolute Damage (BLASTPIS = 6), never negative (the `if`/`then` below). brawn: the Brawn ADD from DamageAdd (VIBKN = 1), signed: Nexus of Power p.104's Gungan Personal Energy Shield prints Brawn -1 (B-1429).

base.description: 'flat' = ranged, value is absolute. 'brawn' = melee/brawl; effective damage = wielder Brawn + value.

crit.description: Critical rating; coerced from string Crit. Lower triggers crits more easily. CORRECTED to minimum 0 at Gate 1: grenades, mines, nets, ion weapons, and tractor beams legitimately carry Crit='0' (no crit rating).

crystal_default.description: OPTIONAL. The attachments.json id of the crystal a ready-made lightsaber HOST is printed with ("a basic lightsaber hilt containing an unmodded Ilum crystal", FaD p.176). When an installed attachment SETS the damage (a crystal), ItemResolve.applyInstalledAttachments PASS 1 takes this crystal's qualities_add off the host before PASS 2 adds the new crystal's, so a replaced crystal's qualities never stack (FaD p.196: one crystal per lightsaber; a removed crystal's qualities are lost). The id must carry a damage_set. Written ONLY by scripts/canonical/apply_weapon_crystal_mods.py from its page-cited CRYSTAL_DEFAULTS manifest (eleven hosts), which validate_registries (1w.crystal) asserts exactly; the hosts that print no default stay without it (ruling f100-b1189-followups-card R-B11FU-5). Registry-only: no saved-character shape carries it.

refuses_crystals.description: OPTIONAL (F-100 M12, ruling f100-m12-census-card R-M12C-64). A host whose page bars lightsaber crystals while its categories still admit the item's other Lightsaber-limited attachments: the lightwhip (Endless Vigil p.43). ItemResolve.attachmentFit refuses every `is_crystal` attachment for it. Absent = the categories alone decide. A narrow member with its first user, not a general exclude grammar.

range.description: Canonical range band, decoded from RangeValue via the RANGE_LABELS map ('wrMedium'->'medium', 'wrEngaged'->'engaged', 'wrClose'->'close'). 'close' is rare for personal weapons (it's the vehicle/sensor-scale band); flag a personal weapon that uses it. Replaces SWItems.rangeLabel — but the map itself survives as shared vocabulary (see _provenance note).

encumbrance.description: Coerced from string Encumbrance. CONFIRMED present (both = 1).

hardpoints.description: Customization hard points; coerced from OggDude field 'HP'. null = source states no capacity (20 weapons); 0 = has slots, none available. Both legal and distinct (R-LBS-3). CONFIRMED present on the reference pair (BLASTPIS 3, VIBKN 2).

price.description: Base price in credits; coerced from string Price. CONFIRMED present (BLASTPIS 400, VIBKN 250).

rarity.description: Rarity rating; coerced from string Rarity. CONFIRMED present (BLASTPIS 4, VIBKN 3).

restricted.description: Restricted/illegal flag. CONFIRMED: OggDude carries `Restricted` as a string 'true'/'false' (or boolean); coerce to boolean, default false when absent (as on BLASTPIS/VIBKN). SWItems reads it as raw.Restricted === 'true' || raw.Restricted === true.

availability.description: Whether this weapon is a player-buyable CATALOG item, an ADVERSARY-specific weapon lifted from an NPC statblock and not generically available (e.g. the Forsaken Jedi's lightsaber, EotE Core p.421, which OggDude folded into its weapons list as a generic 'Lightsaber'), or UNAUDITED (provenance not yet confirmed). OggDude provides NO marker distinguishing catalog gear from lifted adversary equipment, so this is set at ingest — known-adversary entries flagged explicitly, the rest default 'unaudited' pending the catalog-provenance audit, which promotes each to 'catalog' or 'adversary' via the suspect->oracle->human cascade. The player character-creator should show 'catalog' (or 'catalog'+'unaudited' until the audit completes); NPC resolution may reference any. Candidate shared concern across item-like entities (armor/gear/attachments) when the items cluster lands. Optional/absent == 'unaudited'.

type.description: Weapon classification from OggDude Type (e.g. 'Energy Weapon', 'Melee'). For filtering; corroborates damage.base but is not the primary discriminator (DamageAdd presence is).

categories.description: Tag taxonomy from OggDude Categories (BLASTPIS ['Blaster Pistol','Blaster','Pistol','Ranged']; VIBKN ['Cutting Edge Melee','Powered Melee']) for browse/filter/shop generation. Do NOT use these free-text tags to infer damage.base.

qualities.description: Normalized from OggDude Qualities (object | array | absent) into a uniform array. VIBKN -> [{id:'pierce',name:'Pierce',ranked:true,rank:2},{id:'vicious',name:'Vicious',ranked:true,rank:1}]; BLASTPIS -> [{id:'stun_setting',name:'Stun Setting',ranked:false}]. Count is a string to coerce. Replaces SWItems.formatQualities.

ranked.description: True if the quality carries a numeric rank (OggDude Count present); false for binary qualities like Stun Setting.

rank.description: Present if and only if ranked is true; maps from coerced OggDude Count.

sources.description: Books that define this weapon, from OggDude Sources.Source (both records = the three core rulebooks). OggDude carries multiple book NAMES and NO page. Map each name onto a rules-index pdfs.alias at ingest. In-app rule lookup is therefore search-by-name within these books, not a page jump.

_provenance.description: Source tag. OggDude's own Custom flag (e.g. 'DescOnly' on both records) may be captured here if useful. Kept simple because the driver is technical control, not IP; curated text rides the lore-overrides overlay, not this field.

pool_mods.description: Extracted dice-pool modifiers at row level (R-DPS-1). Weapons have no mod objects, so from is absent.

effects.description: Non-dice structured effects at row level (R-DPS-8). Same effect object as base_mods[].effect, referenced by $ref. Weapons carry these at row level because they have no mod objects.

never_modelled.description: Row-level marker for descriptions deliberately not structured (R-DPS-8, R-IEE-3). Records that a human read the description and judged its remainder unmodellable.

_cite.description: Page-granular print citation for a record whose numbers were read off a printed page rather than imported (free text, e.g. 'hobs p.60' or 'aor p.225 (eote p.220, fad p.221)'). Declared by ruling b299-b308-weapon-record-fields R-WRF-1: `sources` carries book NAMES and `_provenance` is a source TAG, so neither can carry a page, and A2-NWG-1's citation duty is page-granular. Absent on imported records, which are attributable through `sources` + `_provenance` instead.

not_purchasable.description: True = the record is not a thing a character can buy. DECLARED AS SHIPPED-DATA DOCUMENTATION ONLY: as of ruling b299-b308-weapon-record-fields (2026-08-26) NO SOURCE CONSUMER READS THIS FIELD -- verified by grep across lib/, player/, gm/, dice/. It is declared so the flag on shipped records is explained rather than mysterious. A future consumer that gives it behaviour cites R-WRF-1 and updates this description; until then, `store_hidden` is the field that actually does something.
